College of Graduate Health Sciences
The UT Health Sciences College of Graduate Health Sciences prepares students for advanced
careers in research, academia, industry, government, and health-related fields. Located
in Memphis, the college offers graduate-level training across biomedical sciences,
health outcomes, epidemiology, pharmaceutical sciences, nursing science, speech and
hearing science, and related disciplines.
Founded in 1928, the College of Graduate Health Sciences offers PhD, Master of Science,
and Master of Dental Science programs, along with certificate and combined-degree
pathways. Students learn in a health science center environment that supports advanced
study, research training, faculty mentorship, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Take the Next Step
Students interested in graduate study at UTHS can explore available programs, review
admissions requirements, request more information, or begin the application process.

Explore Graduate Programs
The College of Graduate Health Sciences offers programs for students interested in
advanced study and research across a range of health science fields.
Program areas include:
Biomedical Engineering
Biomedical Sciences
Dental Sciences
Epidemiology
Health Outcomes and Policy Research
Laboratory Research and Management
Nursing Science
Pharmaceutical Sciences
Pharmacology
Speech and Hearing Science
Students can also explore certificate programs and combined-degree pathways that connect
graduate research training with professional study in other UT Health Sciences colleges.
Why UTHS Graduate Health Sciences?
Graduate students at UTHSC are part of an academic health science center focused on
education, research, clinical care, and service. The College of Graduate Health Sciences
gives students the opportunity to pursue advanced training in areas that connect directly
to human health, biomedical discovery, health policy, patient outcomes, and scientific
innovation.
Through faculty mentorship, research training, and interdisciplinary study, students
prepare for careers that can make an impact across universities, research institutions,
health systems, industry, and government agencies.
Research-Focused Graduate Training
Research is central to the graduate student experience in the College of Graduate
Health Sciences. Students work with faculty across health science disciplines and
develop the skills needed to contribute to scientific discovery, evidence-based practice,
health policy, and biomedical innovation.
This research-focused environment is especially important for students planning to
pursue PhD study, academic research, clinical investigation, pharmaceutical sciences,
biomedical sciences, or health outcomes research.
Frequently Asked Questions
What programs are offered through the UTHS College of Graduate Health Sciences?
The College of Graduate Health Sciences offers PhD, Master of Science, and Master
of Dental Science programs across biomedical, clinical, pharmaceutical, nursing, health
outcomes, and speech and hearing science fields.
Does UTHS offer PhD programs in the health sciences?
Yes. UTHS offers PhD programs through the College of Graduate Health Sciences, including
programs in biomedical sciences, pharmaceutical sciences, nursing science, speech
and hearing science, and related areas.
Does the College of Graduate Health Sciences offer master’s programs?
Yes. The college offers master’s-level programs in several areas, including biomedical
engineering, dental sciences, epidemiology, health outcomes and policy research, laboratory
research and management, and pharmacology.
Are combined-degree programs available?
Yes. UTHS offers combined-degree pathways that connect graduate research training
with professional study in other colleges, including options such as AuD/PhD, DDS/PhD,
DNP/PhD, MD/PhD, and PharmD/PhD.
How do I apply to a graduate program at UTHS?
Students apply online to the specific graduate program they are interested in. Some
programs may have additional requirements, so applicants should review the admissions
details for their intended program.
What careers can graduates pursue?
Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, industry, government, research, health
care, and other fields connected to biomedical science, health outcomes, policy, and
clinical investigation.
